articles.title: Hardwick Tactical Receives Maximum $20.2 Million DLA Air Force Jacket Contract
articles.snippet:
Hardwick Tactical has received a fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract with a maximum value of approximately $20.2 million to produce flame-resistant intermediate-weather jackets for the Air Force.
The post Hardwick Tactical Receives Maximum $20.2 Million DLA Air Force Jacket Contract appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Hardwick Tactical Receives Maximum $20.2 Million DLA Air Force Jacket Contract
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 11:04 AM
Hardwick Tactical Receives Maximum $20.2 Million DLA Air Force Jacket Contract
Hardwick Tactical has received a fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract with a maximum value of approximately $20.2 million to produce flame-resistant intermediate-weather jackets for the Air Force.
The Mayaguez, Puerto Rico-based small business will manufacture intermediate weather outer-layer jackets in sage and operational camouflage pattern configurations.
The five-year contract includes no option periods. Its ordering period will conclude on November 11, 2031.
The procurement was competitive, with one response received. The Defense Logistics Agency reported the acquisition as competitive despite receiving a single offer.
Funding will come from fiscal 2027 through 2032 defense working capital funds. The announcement does not identify an initial order, obligation, or guaranteed minimum amount.
Accordingly, the approximately $20.2 million represents the contract’s maximum ordering ceiling rather than guaranteed revenue to Hardwick Tactical. Actual payments will depend on the quantities DLA orders during the five-year period.
The Air Force is the military customer identified for the garments. Intermediate-weather outer layers provide protection in cooler or changing conditions while allowing service members to perform operational duties.
The flame-resistant requirement is particularly important for personnel working near aircraft, fuel, machinery, or other environments where exposure to fire or thermal hazards may occur.
Offering the garment in sage and operational camouflage pattern versions allows DLA to support different uniform and mission requirements.
DLA Troop Support in Philadelphia is the contracting activity for contract SPE1C1-27-D-0014. The organization manages military clothing and textile supply chains, including the procurement of uniforms, protective apparel, and related materials.
The IDIQ structure gives the agency flexibility to place orders based on inventory levels, deployment requirements, sizing demand, and other operational needs.
The award adds a long-term Air Force apparel contract to Hardwick Tactical’s production portfolio while preserving its federal designation as a small business.

articles.text:
WhiteMatter: $20 Million Series A To Expand Enterprise AI Agent Governance
By Amit Chowdhry
Nov 11, 2026
WhiteMatter: $20 Million Series A To Expand Enterprise AI Agent Governance
WhiteMatter has raised $20 million in Series A funding to expand its enterprise platform for governing autonomous artificial intelligence agents, models, tools, and interactions. Blumberg Capital led the round, with participation from existing investors Crew Capital and Sprout & Oak. WhiteMatter previously operated under the name QuilrAI.
The company developed its platform to address security and operational risks created by AI agents that can access sensitive information, generate content, make decisions, interact with software, and create or influence other agents.
WhiteMatter governs AI across endpoints, browsers, software-as-a-service applications, cloud systems, and code. It assesses agents before deployment, applies policies to their actions, monitors outcomes, and manages traffic and spending through a controlled gateway.
Its architecture can deploy a dedicated Guardian agent for every AI agent operating within a customer’s environment. When autonomous systems create additional agents, WhiteMatter can provision corresponding Guardians to extend policy enforcement.
WhiteMatter has more than 2.25 million agents under management and expects that number to exceed 5.5 million by the end of 2026. Its platform has governed 116 billion AI interactions and helped customers avoid more than 11 trillion tokens during the past nine months.
The company tripled its customer base during 2026 and increased revenue fivefold over six months. It reported approximately 200% net revenue retention with no customer churn.
Customers include Sentara Health, Alter Domus, New American Funding, Concentrix, and other large enterprises. WhiteMatter’s policy architecture delivers decisions in 2.24 milliseconds and can process as many as 7,800 actions per minute.
The new capital will support research, product development, go-to-market expansion, and additions to WhiteMatter’s executive team. The company is positioning its technology as an operational and security layer for businesses deploying AI at scale.

Companies that slow down AI adoption risk being overtaken by competitors that move fast, stay secure, and scale AI with confidence, which is exactly why we built WhiteMatter.”
Vidit Arora, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of WhiteMatter

SPARETECH aims to cut manufacturers' spare parts inventory by 60% within three years with AI that ensures parts are available when they are needed
MUNICH , Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SPARETECH, a provider of enterprise AI for spare parts management, today announced it has raised $20 million in Series B funding to help manufacturers cut their spare parts inventory without risking downtime. Blume Equity and Insight Partners co-led the round, with participation from Headline.
Geographic expansion and growth trajectory
Continue Reading
SPARETECH Founders | Dr. Lukas Biedermann & Martin Weber
SPARETECH has established itself in the United States and grown its revenue fivefold since the start of 2024. Over the same period, the company grew its spare parts catalog to more than 40 million verified parts and expanded its network to 15,000 manufacturer and supplier partners. The global rollout of Nestlé, a SPARETECH customer, put 320 plants across 70 countries live in less than a year, further affirming SPARETECH's global enterprise capabilities and speed.
"Every customer we work with wants the same thing: the production line running with less inventory on the shelf. That is the problem we are going to solve with Maintenance teams, and our goal is to cut spare parts inventory by 60% in the next three years, while securing the same uptime."
Martin Weber, CEO and Co-Founder, SPARETECH
Why spare parts stay on the shelf
Spare parts management has long been one of manufacturing's most persistent inefficiencies. A single stockout can halt production and idle an entire line, making plants default to holding extensive spare parts inventories as a safeguard. The result is a substantial amount of capital sitting on the shelf. SPARETECH's 2026 benchmark report puts the average value of spare parts inventory at $169 million per company.
Source: Unlocking cost savings in spare parts management: The 2026 benchmark report on MRO spend, productivity, and working capital , SPARETECH, 2026.
From visibility to availability
Since its founding, SPARETECH has helped customers gain visibility into the parts they hold and standardize their spare parts data, which is the foundation of effective spare parts management. Meaningfully reducing inventory levels, however, requires more than good data. It requires physical action.
SPARETECH is moving the market beyond insights and recommendations toward measurable outcomes: lower inventory with the same uptime. To reach the 60% goal, every maintenance professional needs confidence that the right part will be available when needed, even if it sits on another company's shelf. SPARETECH's AI will secure that availability.
"Every part sitting idle is cash that could be working somewhere else. We are building AI that makes sure the right part is available when a plant needs it and put those idle parts back into circulation, so the money tied up on the shelf can go back to growing the business."
Dr. Lukas Biedermann, COO and Co-Founder, SPARETECH

Danish biotech specialist raises €20 million to accelerate market-ready trait development
Make us your Google favorite
Danish biotechnology company Traitomic has raised €20 million in a Series A round led by Sofinnova Partners. The investor consortium also includes the Export and Investment Fund of Denmark (EIFO), Footprint Firm, Nordic Foodtech VC, PSV Hafnium and SVG Ventures. The round marks Traitomic's first external investment since its spin-out from Carlsberg and follows the development of a growing customer base across multiple industries. The funding will support international expansion and continued development of the company's scientific and commercial capabilities.
The world increasingly depends on improved biological performance to address challenges in food security, resource efficiency and sustainability. Yet translating a biological need into a commercially relevant trait can be slow, fragmented and difficult to scale. Traitomic helps bridge that gap not only by developing market-ready traits, but also supporting customers from initial commercial challenges through to deployment.
© Traitomic (L-R) Toni Wendt, Technology Lead; Jan Gottlieb, Commercial Lead; Gustav Hambraeus, Managing Director
Traitomic's proprietary FIND-IT platform identifies specific genetic variants in conventionally bred populations without gene editing, enabling rapid trait development while maintaining broad regulatory and commercial applicability. Unlike many trait-development approaches that are tailored to specific organism types, the platform can be applied across both plant and microbial systems.
To date, Traitomic has delivered 116 traits to 47 customers across 32 organisms spanning plant breeding and seed; food supply chain and precision nutrition; and biosolutions and industrial biotech. The projects range from improving crop robustness and yield, to developing differentiated food products with enhanced flavour, nutrition or shelf life, and optimising enzymes and strains used in industrial biotechnology. This breadth of applications reflects demand from customers across multiple industries and highlights the significant opportunity to expand trait development across the broader bioeconomy.
© Traitomic
The funding will support Traitomic's international expansion and help the company capture this opportunity across food, agriculture and biosolutions markets. In addition, Traitomic will continue to broaden its integrated offering, enabling closer collaboration with customers from initial biological or commercial challenges through delivery of market-ready traits.
Gustav Hambraeus, CEO and co-founder, Traitomic said: "This investment marks the beginning of Traitomic's next chapter. Over the past years, we have demonstrated that customers across the food value chain are looking for faster routes from biological insight to commercial impact. With the support of our new investors, we can now expand internationally, deepen our collaboration with customers and bring our integrated approach to trait development to many more innovation challenges."
© Traitomic
Michael Krel, Partner, Sofinnova Partners said: "Traitomic has demonstrated something that is rare in biological innovation: the ability to develop commercially relevant traits across a broad range of organisms and applications. articles.title: US startup raises $20 million for self-assembling spacecraft
articles.snippet: US startup raises $20 million for self-assembling spacecraft mediasat.info
articles.text:
11 Ноя, 2026
Американский стартап привлёк $20 млн на космические аппараты, которые сами собираются на орбите
Новости
Rendezvous Robotics
28 октября стартап Rendezvous Robotics из Голдена в штате Колорадо объявил о посевном раунде на $20 млн. Его возглавили венчурные компании MaC Venture Capital и Toyota Ventures, а средства пойдут на разработку нового поколения аппаратов, лётные демонстрации и расширение команды.
Помимо лидеров, в раунде участвовали фонд University of Michigan Endowment, Astera, Industrious Ventures, Humbition и NextView Ventures. Компанию и дальше поддержали существующие инвесторы Aurelia Foundry, ATX Venture Partners и Mana Ventures.
- Реклама -
Стартап ищет выход из ограничений, которые накладывает запуск. Большинство аппаратов проектируют так, чтобы они поместились в головной обтекатель — защитную оболочку на вершине ракеты, под которой летит груз. Из-за этого ещё до запуска приходится идти на компромиссы в выработке энергии, вычислительных мощностях, размере антенн и теплоотводе, хотя потребность во всём этом растёт.
Гендиректор Джо Лэндон пояснил Payload, что отрасль не хочет аппаратов меньшего размера и меньшей мощности. «Никто не говорит о том, чтобы делать спутники меньше и менее функциональными, — сказал он. — Все хотят больше мощности, больше теплоотвода, более крупные антенны, более чувствительную связь. Но этого не достичь, пока мы не научимся строить прямо в космосе».
Подписывайтесь на Mediasat в Telegram : здесь самые интересные новости из мира технологий
Rendezvous Robotics предлагает другой подход — аппарат из компактных независимых модулей-плиток. Их запускают по отдельности, а на орбите они самостоятельно маневрируют, выравниваются и соединяются в одну конструкцию, которую после запуска можно перестроить под новые задачи. Этот подход вырос из почти десятилетних исследований соосновательницы компании Ариэль Экблау в Массачусетском технологическом институте (MIT) в рамках программы TESSERAE. Ранние поколения TESSERAE уже проверяли на суборбитальной ракете New Shepard компании Blue Origin и во время двух миссий на Международной космической станции (МКС).
Сейчас Rendezvous Robotics разрабатывает новое поколение более крупных независимых модулей, а их движение, выравнивание и сборку проверяет на Земле. Эти испытания продолжат серией параболических полётов в ноябре 2026 года, во время которых самолёт ненадолго создаёт невесомость. В этих полётах испытают электромагнитный привод и движение модулей. Отдельно от них, в декабре на МКС, проведут заключительную демонстрацию TESSERAE пятого поколения — 32 плитки должны автономно собраться в трёхмерную конструкцию.
Демонстрационную миссию на низкой околоземной орбите запланировали не ранее апреля 2028 года. В ней семь независимых модулей должны автономно соединиться в один аппарат, разделиться и снова собраться в иной конфигурации без помощи внешних роботизированных манипуляторов. Компания называет её первой в своём роде и уже зарезервировала место в совместном запуске (rideshare), где модули выведут на орбиту вместе с другими грузами.
Модульность даёт и практическую выгоду. Оператор может менять конфигурацию аппарата, добавлять новые модули или заменять неисправные прямо на орбите, а не строить и запускать новый аппарат. По словам Лэндона, нынешнее обслуживание спутников сводится к продлению срока службы, тогда как система Rendezvous при повреждении может сама изменить свою структуру на лучшую из доступных. Лэндон допускает и создание на орбите склада модулей, кот
